prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 — Policy Summary (≤500 words, ideology-free)

Economy, taxes and pensions
- Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by the end of the Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: state pension and a new age-related personal allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
- Maintain National Living Wage at two-thirds of median earnings; target at c.£13/hour on current forecasts.
- Raise at least £6bn/year by tackling tax avoidance and evasion.
- Child Benefit to be assessed on household income; withdraw between £120k–£160k.

Business, innovation, trade and regulation
- No rise in corporation tax; maintain full expensing and explore extension to leasing.
- SME 10‑point plan: business rates relief, VAT threshold smoothing, better finance (Open Finance, regional mutual banks), lighter reporting, prompt payment enforcement, maintain key tax reliefs, £250m Invest in Women Fund, SME‑focused procurement.
- Public R&D to £22bn/year; invest in AI compute; £4.5bn Advanced Manufacturing Plan; strengthen City reforms; support automotive.
- Complete further FTAs (India, GCC; upgrades with Israel, Switzerland); implement CPTPP; uphold TCA without CJEU alignment.
- Continue post‑Brexit regulatory reform and civil service efficiency measures.

Infrastructure and planning
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, buses); expand gigabit broadband and standalone 5G; support EV charging and sustainable aviation fuel.
- Speed up major infrastructure consent to ~1 year; reform environmental and judicial processes.

Work, welfare and families
- Reform disability benefits (PIP) to better target need; tighten Work Capability Assessment from Sept 2025; overhaul fit notes via specialist assessors.
- Tougher sanctions at 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new fraud powers.
- Childcare: 30 hours free from 9 months by Sept 2025; wraparound care by Sept 2026; Family Hubs in every local authority.

Education, skills and youth
- Mandatory school-day mobile phone bans; parental access to teaching materials.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19; two hours PE weekly; attendance measures.
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑outcome degrees.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 12 months competitive paid military/cyber or part‑time civic roles.

Borders, migration and security
- Legal annual cap on work/family visas that falls each year; pre‑travel health checks; higher fees/IHS.
- Enforce removals to Rwanda; reform asylum rules and pursue returns deals; disrupt smuggling.
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; defence R&D min 5% + 2% exploitation; Ukraine support; Veterans Bill and measures.

NHS and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First, 250 GP builds/modernisations, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental Recovery Plan; service requirement for new dentists; contract reform.
- £3.4bn tech plan (NHS App, AI diagnostics, Federated Data Platform); 5,500 fewer managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco/Vapes Bill; expanded mental health support; implement Cass Review; single‑sex accommodation rights.

Crime, justice and protests
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition and anti-knife powers; officer vetting/licensing; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher community sentencing and fraud measures; new offences (spiking, deepfakes, intimate images).
- Harsher sentences for serious crimes; four new prisons; more foreign national offender removals; court backlog actions.
- Stronger powers on extremist and disruptive protests.

Energy, net zero and bills
- Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; launch CCUS clusters; accelerate nuclear incl. SMRs and Wylfa; import carbon mechanism by 2027.
- No new green levies; maintain price cap; review standing charges; PumpWatch; smart tariffs; £6bn home efficiency plus universal vouchers; consent‑led onshore wind; protect best farmland from solar; no fracking.

Housing
- 1.6m homes; remove nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; fast‑track brownfield in 20 cities; densify inner London; urban development corporations; support SME builders; use Infrastructure Levy for local services.
- Protect Green Belt; permanent first‑time buyer Stamp Duty threshold (£425k); new Help to Buy; CGT relief for sales to sitting tenants; complete leasehold reform; Renters Reform Bill (abolish Section 21 after court reform); controls on holiday lets.

Communities, transport and drivers
- Long‑Term Plan for Towns; extend Community Ownership Fund; more Freeports/Investment Zones; extend £2 bus fare; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; contactless pay‑as‑you‑go nationwide.
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for 20mph/LTNs; powers on pavement parking.

Equality, farming, fisheries, rural and environment
- Clarify Equality Act: sex = biological sex; national school guidance on gender‑questioning pupils and parental rights.
- Farming budget +£1bn (UK‑wide), legal food security target, 50% local/higher‑standard public procurement, fast‑track farm infrastructure, tapered seasonal visas; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.
- Maintain flood defence programme; Plan for Water (sanctions, river recovery network, SW rebate); tree/peatland and urban greening; 11th National Park; waste crime penalties, DRS, halt new incinerators.

Union and devolved
- Continue direct investment in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland; specific transport/energy projects; protect UK internal market; implement Windsor Framework; NI legacy commission.
